chosen_architecture_paradigm: Neuro-symbolic evidence engine: a typed HR knowledge graph whose every cause/effect link carries a verbatim source quote, 10 deterministic Python tools (metrics vs peers, DEMATEL root causes, guardrails, phase scheduling, precedent ranking, ROI) that make every decision, and LLM agents (pillar diagnosticians, skeptic, strategist, jury, report writer on local Mistral-Nemo + OpenRouter) that only choose, quote and explain - checked by a rule+AI plan critic, an audited jury, a two-layer fact-checker and a stability ledger (same input, same answer); FastAPI + React.

diagnosed_root_causes: Employer promise not believed (branding, high confidence): The employer value proposition (EVP) - why someone should work here - is not credible to candidates or staff. Evidence: Brand alignment (promise vs reviews) 46.8 vs sector average 62.1, 25% worse than the sector. Standalone problem that needs its own fix.

Manual spreadsheet tracking (advocacy, high confidence): HR tracks reviews and posts by hand, which costs hours and hides patterns. Evidence: HR hours spent on manual tracking 16 hours/month. Research threshold crossed: HR hours spent on manual tracking is 16, over the >=8 threshold: From 8 hours a month, manual tracking is a material cost that automation recovers. It drives: no financial proof for the board, uneven reputation across sites. Sources: C01, C08, FN3.

Unclear career paths (retention, high confidence): People cannot see how to get promoted or grow. Evidence: Career growth rating 2.52 vs sector average 3.21, 22% worse than the sector. It drives: new hires leaving early, promise vs reality gap. Sources: C05, FN1, R4.

Weak middle management (retention, high confidence): Team managers lack coaching or support, and employees feel it. Evidence: Management rating 2.64 vs sector average 3.34, 21% worse than the sector. It drives: new hires leaving early, promise vs reality gap. Sources: C05, C07, FN1, R4.
